summary: Atsuhiko Yoshida works in religious studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Seikei University, University of Tokyo, Athénée Français, University of Strasbourg, EPHE, and under Georges Dumézil. He held posts at CNRS, University of Geneva, UCLA, Seikei, and Gakushuin University.

Atsuki Nakagami works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Attested affiliations include a guest researcher post at the University of Hamburg (2022) and positions connected with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, University of Tokyo, Rissho University, and Hamburg (attested 2026).
Atsushi Ibuki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (~1978–1989). He served as a professor at Toyo University (attested 2015).

Atsushi Kanazawa specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and held posts at the Meteorological College (lecturer, ~1986–1996) and Komazawa University (assistant professor ~1996–2004; post ~2004).
Atsushi Kiyozawa is an Indologist who completed doctoral coursework at the University of Delhi. He was attested as a lecturer at Kindai University in 1989.

Atsushi Uno specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto and Banaras Hindu universities under teachers including T. R. V. Murti, Raghunath Giri, and Dalsukh Malvania. He held posts at Shuchiin, Kyoto, Tokai, Hiroshima (1974–1986), and Kindai (~1986–1997).

Atsuuji Ashikaga was an Indologist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Doshisha University and Kyoto University under Ryosaburo Sakaki. He held multiple academic posts at Kyoto University (1930–1962) and served at Tokai University (~1967–1975).
Atsuyoshi Keika is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who held posts at Otani University as a lecturer (attested 1990) and professor (attested 2014).

August Boeckh was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg under F. A. Wolf and F. Schleiermacher. Boeckh taught at Heidelberg University (1807–1811) and the University of Berlin/Humboldt University of Berlin (~1810/1811–1861/1867).

August Conrady was a scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and Indology who studied at Würzburg and Leipzig. He held academic posts at Leipzig from 1891, becoming professor in 1920 and chair in 1922, and taught at Peking University (1903–1904).

August Ferdinand Naeke was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Leipzig (~1806–1809) and held posts at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1817–1818) and the University of Bonn (~1818–1838).

August Fick was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Göttingen (1852–1856) under Theodor Benfey. He later served as an extraordinary professor at Göttingen (1876) and ordinary professor at the University of Breslau (1887–1891).
August Fischer was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied at Halle-Wittenberg (~1884–1889). He served on the faculty of the University of Leipzig (~1900–1930).

August Friedrich Pott was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Göttingen and Berlin under Franz Bopp. After lecturing in Berlin (1830), he held a professorship in general linguistics at Halle-Wittenberg from 1833, becoming full professor in 1838.

August Hermann Francke was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at the Moravian teacher seminar in Niesky, Moravian College, and Humboldt University of Berlin, where he later served as Privatdozent (1922) and extraordinary professor (1925).

August Hjalmar Edgren was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Uppsala, Cornell, Nebraska-Lincoln, and Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He held teaching posts at Yale (1874–1880), Lund (1880–1884), Nebraska-Lincoln (~1885–1891), and served as Rector at Gothenburg (1891–1893).

August Johan Bernet Kempers was an archaeologist, historian, and Indologist who studied at Leiden University (~1926–1933). He directed the Archaeological Service of Indonesia (~1936–1953) and held posts at the Netherlands Open Air Museum and the University of Amsterdam.

August Leskien was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Kiel, Leipzig, and Jena under August Schleicher and Georg Curtius. He taught at Göttingen and Jena, and was a professor of Slavic philology at Leipzig from 1870 until 1915.

August Schleicher was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig, Tübingen, Erlangen, and Bonn under Heinrich Ewald and Friedrich Ritschl. He held posts at Bonn (1846), Charles University (1850–1857), and the University of Jena (from 1857).
August Sundin is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar attested in 2026 as a PhD student and faculty member at Ghent University.
